summary:
[  edit  ]
NOTE
OS:  This operator is only supported under the  Microsoft Windows  operating system.
Hardware:  This operator uses the Augmented Reality (AR) SDK of the Nvidia Maxine system and requires a 20, 30, 40 or 50 series Nvidia RTX card to operate.
The models for this operator are not included with TouchDesigner. To use this operator you will need to download the 0.8.7 version AR SDK for your  GPU  from  https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce/broadcasting/broadcast-sdk/resources/ .
The Face Track  CHOP  can detect faces and facial landmark points in an image, as well as the direction the face is looking relative to the camera. Using a compatible 3D Morphable Face Model (3DMM) and the  Face Track SOP , it can also be used to fit and animate a 3D mesh to the detected face.
The input image is taken from a provided  TOP  and can be of any resolution or format, and either a still image or video. If multiple faces are present in an image, the  CHOP  will attempt to track the largest one detected.
The coordinates of the detected features are given in u, v positions relative to the bottom-left corner of the input image. By default, the values range from 0 to 1, but the 'Aspect Correct' parameter can be enabled to scale the values so that they can be used as 3D coordinates while maintaining the aspect ratio of the original image.
Tip : Look at the several examples of the Face Track  CHOP / SOP  in  OP Snippets .
To align a 3D rendering of the points with the original input image, set the 'Projection' of your  Camera COMP  to 'Orthographic', the 'Ortho Origin' parameter to 'Bottom-Left', and the 'Ortho Width' to 1, while also enabling 'Aspect Correct' on the Face Track  CHOP .
To use the mesh fitting features you will need a compatible face mesh file in the Nvidia ' nvf ' format. We recommend using the  face_model2.nvf  file that is now included in the  Config/Models  folder inside your TouchDesigner installation.  Note:  Mesh files generated for previous versions of TouchDesigner will no longer work.
See also:  Face Track SOP

parameters.label: Active
parameters.name: active
parameters.description: Enables the face tracking features.

parameters.label: Model  Folder
parameters.name: modelfolder
parameters.description: The location of the AI model files used for face detection. By default these files are located in the Config/Models folder.

parameters.label: Mesh File
parameters.name: meshfile
parameters.description: The 3D morphable mesh file in Nvidia 'nvf' format to use in mesh fitting. When available, the fitted mesh can be accessed with a  Face Track SOP .

parameters.label: TOP
parameters.name: top
parameters.description: A path to the  TOP  operator that will provides the image to perform face tracking on.

parameters.label: Bounding Boxes
parameters.name: bbox
parameters.description: Output channels that describe a bounding box around the detected face. The channels give the u and v positions of the center of the face as well as the width and height of the box. The positions are relative to the bottom-left corner of the input image.

parameters.label: Bounding Box Confidence
parameters.name: bboxconfidence
parameters.description: Outputs a channel that describes the level of certainty that the AI model has detected a face in the input image. Higher numbers indicate greater confidence.

parameters.label: Rotations
parameters.name: rotations
parameters.description: Output rx, ry, and rz values that indicate how the face is oriented in the image. (0,0,0) indicates that the face is oriented directly towards the camera. Values can range from +/- 180 degrees as the subject turns away from the camera.

parameters.label: None
parameters.name: none
parameters.description: The number of facial landmark points to output. Points are numbered beginning from 1 and always represent a fixed feature on the face such as the chin, eyebrow, nose, etc. Positions are given as u and v coordinates relative to the bottom-left corner of the input image.

parameters.label: 68 (Multi-PIE Mark-ups)
parameters.name: num68
parameters.description: A standard set of facial landmark features used in AI research.  See Reference Diagram.

parameters.name: num126
parameters.description: An extended set of landmark features.

parameters.label: Landmark Confidence
parameters.name: landmarkconfidence
parameters.description: Adds a confidence value for each landmark feature. Higher values indicate the feature is more likely to be accurate.

parameters.label: Mesh Transform
parameters.name: meshtransform
parameters.description: Enable to output translate, rotate and scale channels for the fitted face mesh. This feature requires a valid 3D morphable face mesh file (see notes above). The values from these channels can be used to transform the mesh produced by an attached  Face Track SOP  so that it aligns with the input image. By default the fitted mesh is pre-transformed to align with the image, but if 'Pre-Transform' is disabled in the  SOP , these values can be used instead for more control and speed.

parameters.label: Aspect Correct UVs
parameters.name: aspectcorrectuv
parameters.description: Rescales the the u and v positions so that they have the correct aspect ratio of the input image. This is useful when using the u, v positions as 3D coordinates rather than as image positions.

parameters.label: Time Slice
parameters.name: timeslice
parameters.description: Turning this on forces the channels to be " Time Sliced ".  A  Time Slice  is the time between the last cook frame and the current cook frame.

parameters.label: Scope
parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: To determine which channels get affected, some CHOPs use a  Scope  string on the Common page.

parameters.label: Sample Rate  Match
parameters.name: srselect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Handle cases where multiple input CHOPs' sample rates are different. When Resampling occurs, the curves are interpolated according to the Interpolation Method Option, or "Linear" if the Interpolate Options are not available.

parameters.label: Resample At First Input's Rate
parameters.name: first
parameters.description: Use rate of first input to resample others.

parameters.label: Resample At Maximum Rate
parameters.name: max
parameters.description: Resample to the highest sample rate.

parameters.label: Resample At Minimum Rate
parameters.name: min
parameters.description: Resample to the lowest sample rate.

parameters.label: Error If Rates Differ
parameters.name: err
parameters.description: Doesn't accept conflicting sample rates.

parameters.label: Export  Method
parameters.name: exportmethod
parameters.description: ⊞  - This will determine how to connect the  CHOP  channel to the parameter. Refer to the  Export  article for more information.

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Index
parameters.name: datindex
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the index of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Name
parameters.name: datname
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the name of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: Channel Name is  Path : Parameter
parameters.name: autoname
parameters.description: The channel is the full destination of where to export to, such has  geo1/transform1:tx .

parameters.label: Export   Root
parameters.name: autoexportroot
parameters.description: This path points to the root node where all of the paths that exporting by  Channel Name is  Path : Parameter   are relative to.

parameters.label: Export  Table
parameters.name: exporttable
parameters.description: The  DAT  used to hold the export information when using the  DAT  Table  Export  Methods (See above).

parameters.label: start
parameters.description: Start of the  CHOP  interval in samples.

parameters.label: length
parameters.description: Number of samples in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: sample_rate
parameters.description: The samplerate of the channels in frames per second.

parameters.label: num_channels
parameters.description: Number of channels in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: time_slice
parameters.description: 1 if  CHOP  is  Time Slice  enabled, 0 otherwise.

parameters.label: export_sernum
parameters.description: A count of how often the export connections have been updated.

parameters.label: total_cooks
parameters.description: Number of times the operator has cooked since the process started.

parameters.label: cook_time
parameters.description: Duration of the last cook in milliseconds.

parameters.label: cook_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the component timeline.

parameters.label: cook_abs_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the absolute time.

parameters.label: cook_start_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator started cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cook_end_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator finished cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cooked_this_frame
parameters.description: 1 if operator was cooked this frame.

parameters.label: warnings
parameters.description: Number of warnings in this operator if any.

parameters.label: errors
parameters.description: Number of errors in this operator if any.

parameters.label: The Graphics Processing Unit. This is the high
parameters.description: speed, many-core processor of the graphics card/chip that takes geometry, images and data from the CPU and creates images and processed data.

parameters.label: samples
parameters.description: per-second of a  CHOP . Each CHOP in your network has a sample rate. In contrast, the overall timeline has a  Frame Rate , which is the number of frames to  cook  and display per second, generally your monitor display frequency, default 60.

parameters.label: An  Operator Family  that manipulates text strings: multi
parameters.description: line text or tables. Multi-line text is often a python  Script  or  GLSL  Shader, but can be any multi-line text.  Tables  are rows and columns of cells, each containing a text string.

parameters.label: TouchDesigner is a hierarchy of components. "root" is the top
parameters.description: most network in the hierarchy. The  Network Path  or Path for root is simply  / . A typical path is  /project1/moviein1 .
